summary: The article accurately reports on the Finance Ministry's directive regarding delayed NPS contributions, including the compensatory interest rate and accountability measures. However, some tax deduction limits for NPS contributions are not entirely precise or complete.

claims.claim: Employers must pay interest to subscribers if their NPS contributions are credited past the due date.
claims.note: The Department of Expenditure (DoE) under the Ministry of Finance has issued an office memorandum stating this.

claims.claim: This compensatory interest will be calculated at the prevailing Public Provident Fund (PPF) interest rate.
claims.note: The DoE memorandum specifies that the interest will match the prevailing PPF interest rate.

claims.claim: The current PPF interest rate, which will be used for compensation, stands at 7.1% per annum.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the current PPF interest rate as 7.1% per annum for Q1 FY 2025-26 and Q2 FY 2024-25.

claims.claim: Employer's contribution (up to 10% of basic salary plus dearness allowance is tax-deductible for the employer).
claims.note: Employer contributions are deductible up to 10% of salary (basic + dearness allowance) for private sector employees under the old tax regime. For central government employees, it's up to 14%. Under the new tax regime, it can be up to 14% for all employees.

claims.claim: Employee contributions to NPS are eligible for deductions under Section 80CCD(1) within the overall limit of Section 80C.
claims.note: Section 80CCD(1) allows deductions for individual contributions to NPS, limited to 10% of salary (basic + DA) for salaried individuals, and this is part of the overall ₹1.5 lakh limit under Section 80C.

claims.claim: Employer contributions are eligible for deduction under Section 80CCD(2), up to 10% of salary (basic + DA), which is over and above the ₹1.5 lakh limit of Section 80C.
claims.note: Employer contributions under Section 80CCD(2) are indeed over and above the Section 80C limit. The deduction limit is up to 10% of salary (basic + DA) for private sector employees and up to 14% for central government employees.

claims.claim: If your employer refuses to pay the compensatory interest, you can escalate it through the PFRDA's grievance redressal mechanism, which can be accessed via the NPS Trust website.
claims.note: PFRDA has a grievance redressal mechanism, including the 'Pension Sahayak' portal, for subscribers to raise complaints.

article_title: NPS Remittance Delays: Finance Ministry Mandates Interest for Late Credits
